cells.tense: You are quietly holding up your share of what means something here.
cells.ask: Hand one thing on this week — a recipe, a word, a tool, a story — and let it go without checking what they do with it.
cells.core:
You are carrying the thing that matters here, and carrying it well. You know what to keep and how to keep it: the language, the ritual, the dish, the one you bring. It arrives for other people with a steadiness they don't have to think about.

The way this holds is not to grip harder. It is to carry the thing without squeezing it into a shape it didn't have — something that contains rather than crushes. That has a cost: no one thanks a load that doesn't drop. To feed it, hand one piece on. Notice what you sent, and let that be enough.

cells.verb: carrying what you were given, unglamorously and on time

cells.tense: You are standing over the safety of a thing that has not been taken from you yet.
cells.ask: Pick what you are holding tonight and leave it with one other person for that evening, then pick it up the next morning.
cells.core:
You are bracing over it. You get there before the need does, gripping the tradition so hard that the custom turns into a rule just to make sure it survives. Somewhere ahead you are carrying a loss that hasn't arrived. You hold what you were given as if the next handoff might be the last one.

Steadfastness isn't the same as setting it down for good. Something that contains a thing — lets another hand touch it, lets it be done a little differently — is what outlives the one holding it. The tighter grip isn't the answer. Let what you keep travel once. Name the piece you're gripping, and set it down for an evening.

cells.tense: You have stopped offering what is held to the people it belongs to.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you carry from those before you — a phrase, a dish, a habit — and tell one person why it stayed with you.
cells.core:
Working, what you carry stays in motion. A recipe gets made and handed over, a phrase gets used in front of someone, a way of marking a date gets shown to a friend who didn't know it. That is the shape of it: material moving by your hand into another person's life, and nothing lost in the leaving.

What you have now is the still version. The material is there — a phrase from your family, a dish, a habit — and it stays where it is. So the fix isn't to work up belief first. Make one piece visible to one person, once, and put its story beside it. You're not asking to be certain; you're asking to be seen holding it.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the family thing going, and you talk about it as if it keeps itself.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you carried this month and say to the person it reaches, "I brought this forward for you."
cells.core:
You open the calendar nobody else opens, start the recipe nobody else starts, repeat the language nobody else repeats. It reaches people as ordinary, dependable, already there — and that is the shape of this working well. The effort is yours, and it lands.

What is off is that you pass it on as if it stayed alive by itself. Say what you hold is yours to keep and keep passing. And if this traveled a long way to reach you, let the fact that you chose it count. Name one piece of effort to the person it reaches, once.
